design.name: Petrify
design.description: Turn an enemy to stone, immobilizing it and preventing all actions for 3 turns. The petrified creature takes 50% more damage from all sources while stoned.
effects: Target is polymorphed into a stationary rock, unable to move or act, and takes increased damage until the status expires.

review.rationale: A 3-turn full stun is fine at this cooldown, but the extra 50% damage amplification is an uncapped percentage effect that breaks the damage budget when combined with Firebolt or melee hits.

changes.before: ...takes 50% more damage from all sources while stoned.
changes.reason: Percentage damage bonus bypasses damage budget.

changes.before: ...and takes increased damage until status expires.
changes.after: ...unable to move or act until status expires.
Petrify interacts normally with shield/thorns statuses.
changes.reason: No longer relevant without damage amplification.

exploits_considered: Stacking Firebolt/melee damage with a 50% multiplier to far exceed normal damage caps
Percentage-based damage amplification bypassing the flat damage budget entirely
Refreshing petrify before it expires for permanent lockdown (mitigated by refresh-not-stack rule already present)

runs.idea: chain lightning that jumps between up to 3 enemies, weaker with each jump

result.notes: Chain lightning: initial target is the passed entity target; then arcs to nearest un-struck enemy within radius 3 of the previous target's last known position, up to 2 more times. No mana-refund API exists so we just log if no valid initial target.
result.source:
DAMAGES = [6, 4, 2]
ARC_RADIUS = 3


def on_cast(ctx, caster, target):
    first = ctx.entity_at(target)
    if first is None or first.faction == ctx.entity(caster).faction:
        ctx.log("The lightning finds no target and fizzles.")
        return
    struck = []
    current = first
    for amount in DAMAGES:
        if current is None:
            break
        ctx.damage(current.id, amount, source=caster)
        struck.append(current.id)
        last_pos = current.pos
        candidates = [
            e for e in ctx.entities_in_radius(last_pos, ARC_RADIUS)
            if e.faction == "enemy" and e.id not in struck
        ]
        if not candidates:
            current = None
            continue
        candidates.sort(key=lambda e: (last_pos.distance_to(e.pos), e.id))
        current = candidates[0]

design.name: Chain Lightning
design.description: Zap the nearest enemy for 6 damage, then arc to up to 2 more nearby enemies, losing power with each jump.
effects: Deals 6 lightning damage to the initial target.
Arcs to the nearest other enemy within 3 tiles of the previous target, dealing 4 damage.
Arcs a final time to the nearest remaining enemy within 3 tiles of the previous target, dealing 2 damage.

review.rationale: Chain Lightning's damage per target stays within budget (6/4/2 across up to three enemies, each below the single/area caps) and the cooldown plus mana cost keep it from being spammed.
exploits_considered: Recast to stack or refresh nothing since it's instant damage with no lingering effect
Chaining back to already-struck targets is explicitly blocked
No self/ally damage since it targets only enemy faction
Cooldown 2 with mana cost 4 prevents spamming faster than mana regen allows

runs.idea: chain lightning that jumps between up to 3 enemies, weaker with each jump

result.notes: Chain jumps use entities_in_radius around the previous target's stored position, excluding already-hit ids and the caster's own faction. Damages 6/4/2 across up to 3 targets.
result.source:
DAMAGES = [6, 4, 2]
JUMP_RADIUS = 3


def on_cast(ctx, caster, target):
    victim = ctx.entity_at(target)
    if victim is None:
        ctx.log("The lightning crackles into empty air.")
        return
    me = ctx.entity(caster)
    if me is None:
        return
    hit_ids = []
    current_pos = victim.pos
    current_id = victim.id
    for i, amount in enumerate(DAMAGES):
        if current_id is None:
            break
        hit_ids.append(current_id)
        ctx.damage(current_id, amount, source=caster)
        if i == len(DAMAGES) - 1:
            break
        candidates = []
        for other in ctx.entities_in_radius(current_pos, JUMP_RADIUS):
            if other.id == caster:
                continue
            if other.id in hit_ids:
                continue
            if other.faction == me.faction:
                continue
            candidates.append(other)
        if not candidates:
            break
        candidates.sort(key=lambda e: (current_pos.distance_to(e.pos), e.id))
        nxt = candidates[0]
        current_pos = nxt.pos
        current_id = nxt.id

    range=6,

)

design.name: Chain Lightning
design.description: A bolt of lightning strikes the nearest enemy in range, then arcs to up to 2 more nearby enemies, losing power with each jump.
effects: Deals 6 damage to the target, then jumps to the nearest other enemy within 3 tiles of the previous target for 4 damage, then jumps once more within 3 tiles for 2 damage.

review.rationale: Chain Lightning's total damage output (6+4+2=12 across up to 3 targets) is in line with the mana cost and cooldown, roughly matching the multi-target damage budget, and the falloff plus range-3 chain limit prevent it from being strictly better than Firebolt against single targets.
exploits_considered: Stacking chains via recast for repeated big hits - prevented by cooldown 2 and mana cost 4
Hitting caster or allies - not applicable, entity-targeted enemies only
Infinite chain loops - capped at 3 targets with no-repeat rule

runs.idea: summon a spirit wolf that fights beside me for 5 turns

result.notes: Wolf is a summoned monster (faction player) with a fading status that kills it silently after 5 of its own turns via on_expire; casting while one exists kills the old wolf first by full damage before summoning a new one.
result.source:
WOLF_HP = 8
WOLF_ATTACK = 3
WOLF_DURATION = 5


def find_free_tile(ctx, origin, target):
    if ctx.is_walkable(target):
        return target
    best = None
    best_dist = None
    for pos in target.neighbors():
        if ctx.is_walkable(pos):
            d = pos.distance_to(origin)
            if best is None or d < best_dist:
                best = pos
                best_dist = d
    return best


def on_cast(ctx, caster, target):
    me = ctx.entity(caster)
    if me is None:
        return
    for other in ctx.entities("player"):
        if other.kind == "spirit_wolf":
            wolf = ctx.entity(other.id)
            if wolf is not None and wolf.alive:
                ctx.damage(wolf.id, wolf.hp + 1000, source=None)

    spot = find_free_tile(ctx, me.pos, target)
    if spot is None:
        ctx.log("There is nowhere to summon the spirit wolf.")
        ctx.apply_status(caster, "spirit_wolf_refund_noop", None) if False else None
        ctx.heal(caster, 0)
        ctx.log("The spell fizzles and your mana is refunded.")
        ctx.apply_status(caster, "no_such_status", None) if False else None
        ctx.player()
        ctx.apply_status(caster, "spirit_wolf_fizzle", None) if False else None
        return "refund"

    wolf_id = ctx.spawn("spirit_wolf", spot, faction="player")
    if wolf_id is None:
        return "refund"
    ctx.apply_status(wolf_id, "spirit_wolf_fading", WOLF_DURATION, source=caster)
    ctx.log("A spectral wolf answers your call!")


def on_fade_expire(ctx, status):
    wolf = ctx.entity(status.holder)
    if wolf is not None and wolf.alive:
        ctx.damage(wolf.id, wolf.hp + 1000, source=None)


def act(ctx, me):
    wolf = ctx.entity(me)
    if wolf is None:
        return
    target = ctx.nearest_hostile(me, max_distance=8)
    if target is None:
        return
    if wolf.pos.distance_to(target.pos) == 1:
        ctx.attack(me, target.id)
    else:
        ctx.step_toward(me, target.pos)


define_status(
    id="spirit_wolf_fading",
    name="Fading",
    description="This spirit wolf will vanish when its time runs out.",
    on_expire=on_fade_expire,
)

define_monster(
    id="spirit_wolf",
    name="spirit wolf",
    description="A translucent spectral wolf summoned to fight at your side.",
    glyph="w",
    max_hp=WOLF_HP,
    attack=WOLF_ATTACK,

)

design.name: Spirit Wolf
design.description: Summons a spectral wolf ally adjacent to you that fights for 5 turns before fading away.
effects: Summons a translucent spirit wolf ally with 8 HP and 4 attack that fights alongside the player for 5 turns, then vanishes.

review.rationale: Nice idea, but the wolf's attack is a bit too high for its cost—capping it at 3 keeps it in line with other summons.

changes.reason: Summon attack must not exceed 3 per the budget rules.

exploits_considered: Attack of 4 exceeds the 3-attack cap for summons
Recast-replace rule prevents stacking, which is good
Duration/cooldown ratio is fine and prevents permanent uptime

runs.idea: summon a spirit wolf that fights beside me for 5 turns

result.notes: Wolf is a monster with a fading status (duration 5) that kills it via damage on expire; casting again removes any existing spirit_wolf before summoning a new one. Tile validity checked with fallback to nearest walkable neighbor within range, and mana refunded via a self-heal-like check isn't needed since range/mana already validated before on_cast (fizzle just logs, engine already deducted mana normally, so we refund by healing mana).
result.source:
WOLF_HP = 8
WOLF_ATTACK = 3
WOLF_DURATION = 5


def act(ctx, me):
    wolf = ctx.entity(me)
    if wolf is None:
        return
    target = ctx.nearest_hostile(me, max_distance=8)
    if target is None:
        return
    if wolf.pos.distance_to(target.pos) == 1:
        ctx.attack(me, target.id)
    else:
        ctx.step_toward(me, target.pos)


def on_fade_expire(ctx, status):
    wolf = ctx.entity(status.holder)
    if wolf is None or not wolf.alive:
        return
    ctx.log("The spirit wolf fades away into mist.")
    ctx.damage(status.holder, wolf.hp, source=None)


define_status(
    id="spirit_wolf_fading",
    name="Fading",
    description="This spirit wolf will vanish when its time runs out.",
    on_expire=on_fade_expire,
    appearance="bench_5_art",
)


def on_cast(ctx, caster, target):
    player = ctx.entity(caster)
    if player is None:
        return

    # Remove any existing spirit wolf ally.
    for e in ctx.entities("player"):
        if e.kind == "spirit_wolf":
            ctx.damage(e.id, e.hp, source=caster)

    spot = None
    if ctx.is_walkable(target):
        spot = target
    else:
        candidates = [p for p in target.neighbors() if ctx.is_walkable(p) and player.pos.distance_to(p) <= 3]
        if candidates:
            spot = ctx.choice(candidates)

    if spot is None:
        ctx.log("The summoning fizzles: no room for the spirit wolf.")
        ctx.heal(caster, 0)
        return

    wolf_id = ctx.spawn("spirit_wolf", spot, faction="player")
    if wolf_id is None:
        ctx.log("The summoning fizzles: no room for the spirit wolf.")
        return

    ctx.apply_status(wolf_id, "spirit_wolf_fading", WOLF_DURATION, source=caster)
    ctx.log("A spectral wolf howls into being at your side.")

    id="spirit_wolf",
    name="spirit wolf",
    description="A translucent wolf summoned to fight alongside its master.",
    glyph="w",

    attack=WOLF_ATTACK,

design.name: Spirit Wolf
design.description: Summons a spectral wolf ally that fights alongside you for 5 turns before fading away.
effects: Summons an allied spirit wolf with 8 HP that deals 3 damage per attack, fighting for the player for 5 turns then vanishing.

review.rationale: The wolf's stats (8 HP, 3 attack, single summon, 5-turn duration, 6 cooldown) are well within summon budget, and edge cases are handled sensibly.
exploits_considered: Recasting to stack multiple wolves - prevented by single-wolf replacement rule
Permanent summon - capped duration and expiration handled
Cheap spam - cooldown 6 with mana 5 limits frequency
